edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: After myocardial infarction, beta blockade blunts catecholamine-driven arrhythmias, lowers oxygen demand, and reduces recurrent ischemic stress, which is why a survival benefit is biologically plausible in the post-MI setting.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2026 Al-Shammari meta analysis in Am Heart J Plus already points to beta blockers tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
